Practitioner (placeholder)

Stands in for a practitioner on the care team the scenario runs under. The loader substitutes a real one.

Practitioner for telma, assigned on a care team for telma.
Practitioner kpro

Practitioner for kpro, assigned on a care team for kpro.
Practitioner fob

Practitioner for fob, assigned on a care team for fob.
Practitioner telesaar

Practitioner for telesaar, assigned on a care team for telesaar.

Region Midtjylland

Owner of the plan, its activities, the questionnaire and the automated-processing rules.
Region Nordjylland

Managing organization for the episodes of care and the care teams that deliver the monitoring.

Episode of care (completed)

A completed episode of care for the same patient and the same COPD diagnosis, which ran for about four and a half months and closed well before the open one opened. Shows the closed period and the full status history that a finished episode carries.
Episode of care

The open episode of care the monitoring plan is delivered under, addressing the COPD diagnosis.

Care plan (completed)

The monitoring plan as delivered under the completed episode of care. Status completed, with the full status history and — following the environment's behaviour — a period that is left open.

Closing (scheduled) — completed

Guidance screen shown after the scheduled round is complete.
Head activity (extra) — completed

The container for the unscheduled branch.
Pulse (extra) — completed

The unscheduled pulse measurement, with the same four absolute reference ranges as the scheduled one.
Questionnaire (extra) — completed

The unscheduled symptom questionnaire. This is the request a test questionnaire response is most easily submitted against, since it is not bound to a window.
Saturation and pulse device group (extra) — completed

Groups the unscheduled saturation and pulse measurements as one device group.
Oxygen saturation (extra) — completed

The unscheduled oxygen saturation measurement, with the same absolute reference ranges as the scheduled one. A submission against this request can be made at any time.
Head activity (scheduled) — completed

The container for the scheduled branch. Nothing is submitted against it; it groups the activities below.
Introduction (scheduled) — completed

Guidance screen shown at the start of the scheduled measurement round.
Pulse (scheduled) — completed

The scheduled pulse measurement. Carries four absolute reference ranges, so both a low and a high value triage red: red at or below 50/min and at or above 130/min, yellow in between.
Questionnaire (scheduled) — completed

The scheduled symptom questionnaire. A questionnaire response is submitted against this request and triaged on its answer significance.
Saturation and pulse device group (scheduled) — completed

Groups the saturation and pulse measurements as one device group, so both are taken from the same device in one go.
Saturation and pulse introduction (scheduled) — completed

Guidance screen introducing the saturation and pulse measurements.
Saturation and pulse preparation (scheduled) — completed

Guidance screen telling the patient how to prepare before measuring.
Oxygen saturation (scheduled) — completed

The scheduled oxygen saturation measurement. Carries the absolute reference ranges its triage rule compares a submitted value against: red at or below 85%, yellow from 85% to 88%.

Pulse 118/min (completed episode)

Pulse submitted under the completed episode. 118/min falls in the upper yellow range of 110 to 130, so triage returns yellow and raises a task with priority urgent.
Oxygen saturation 84% (completed episode)

Oxygen saturation submitted under the completed episode. 84% is at or below the red absolute range of 85%, so triage returns red and raises a task with priority asap.
Pulse 72/min (open episode)

Pulse submitted against the unscheduled branch of the open episode's care plan. 72/min falls between the low and high ranges, so triage returns green and the resulting task is routine.

COPD monitoring plan (oxygen saturation, pulse and questionnaire)

COPD monitoring plan with a scheduled mon/wed/fri branch and an unscheduled extra branch, each carrying the saturation and pulse device group and the symptom questionnaire. One submission against the extra branch yields one questionnaire response and two observations.
Closing

Closing guidance for a scheduled round.
Extra head activity

Container for the unscheduled saturation, pulse and questionnaire.
Extra pulse

Unscheduled heart rate, with the same absolute thresholds as the scheduled one.
Extra questionnaire

Unscheduled Master Questionnaire activity, composed of the same questionnaire as the scheduled one.
Extra oxygen saturation and pulse (same device group)

The unscheduled same-device group.
Extra oxygen saturation

Unscheduled oxygen saturation, with the same absolute thresholds as the scheduled one.
Head activity

Container for the scheduled saturation, pulse and questionnaire.
Introduction

Opening guidance for a scheduled round.
Pulse

Heart rate, triaged against absolute thresholds: red at or below 50 and at or above 130, yellow either side of the 60-110 green band.
Questionnaire

Master Questionnaire activity presenting the symptom questionnaire, the single questionnaire of this plan.
Oxygen saturation and pulse (same device group)

The same-device group: one pulse oximeter, one patient action, two values. Its children are the saturation and the pulse.
Oxygen saturation and pulse measurement

Guidance shown before the saturation and pulse measurement: warm the hands, and what the reading involves.
Preparation

Immediate preparation: sit still for five minutes beforehand and keep the hand steady during the reading.
Oxygen saturation

Oxygen saturation, triaged against absolute thresholds: red at or below 85%, yellow up to 88%, green above.
COPD questionnaire

COPD symptom questionnaire: treatment status, three symptom scales, sputum colour and a conditional comment. Eighteen answer-significance mappings across green, yellow and red.
observation-absolute-range-triage

Triages a submitted observation against absolute thresholds expressed in the observation's own unit. Reads the reference ranges from the observation it is given, so a measurement must carry them to be assessed; a GAL range yields a yellow assessment and a RAL range a red one.
questionnaire-response-triage-on-answersignificance

Triages a submitted questionnaire response by matching each answer against the answer-significance mappings on the questionnaire, and recording one finding basis per answered question alongside the overall assessment.

Loader settings

Read by the loader, never loaded. anchorDate is the day the scenario is written for: it maps to the load date, and every date in the data shifts by the same number of days. Table pairing the coexistence tag with the programme it runs: the loader substitutes ${COEXISTENCE_TAG} and ${EHEALTH_PROGRAM} together, making one copy of the vendor-scoped data per vendor listed here.
Loader code systems

Read by the loader, never loaded. The ehealth-system and ehealth-program CodeSystems of dk.ehealth.sundhed.fhir.ig.core: the loader checks the coexistence tags against them, and adds any codes the terminology service lacks.
